data.title: Amino acid homeostasis by CORVET/HOPS: A metabolic and stress resilience checkpoint for T cells
data.authors: Wang J; Ni Z; Zhang Xinxin; He L; Cheng X; Huang L; Ye H; Li P; Zhao TJ; Du X
data.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.model_system: Mouse T cells (conditional VPS18 / VPS11 knockout, in vitro and in vivo)
data.finding: Identifies the CORVET and HOPS endolysosomal tethering complexes as upstream suppliers of intracellular amino acids in activated T cells, acquired via macropinocytosis. Loss of the core subunits VPS18 or VPS11 starves the cell of amino acids, switches on the integrated stress response and shuts down mTORC1; enforced mTORC1 activity rescues the proliferative defect while BIM deletion rescues survival, separating the two failure modes. Places vesicular nutrient acquisition upstream of the canonical lysosomal amino-acid-sensing arm of mTORC1.
data.abstract_excerpt: Amino acid sufficiency is critical for T cell metabolic reprogramming, yet how T cells maintain amino acid homeostasis remains poorly defined. Here, we identify the CORVET and HOPS (CORVET/HOPS) tethering complexes as essential upstream regulators. In activated T cells, they sustain intracellular amino acid levels by promoting macropinocytosis to acquire extracellular nutrients. This function enables dual signaling outcomes: suppression of the integrated stress response (ISR) and activation of mTORC1, which together license metabolic plasticity and effector function.

extracted_findings.intervention: Genetic ablation of CORVET/HOPS subunits VPS18 or VPS11; BIM deletion; enforced mTORC1 activity
extracted_findings.target: CORVET/HOPS tethering complexes; mTORC1; integrated stress response
extracted_findings.species: Mouse (T cells, in vitro and in vivo)
extracted_findings.effect: CORVET/HOPS loss causes amino acid scarcity, ISR activation and mTORC1 failure, abrogating T cell immunity
